key_insight: ATSplat brings the adaptive density allocation of traditional 3D Gaussian Splatting into a compact feed-forward model. Instead of tying primitives to input pixels, it learns to expand tokens where the scene needs more detail, enabling better quality without heavy per-viewpoint dependence.
problem_solved: Existing feed-forward 3DGS methods usually place Gaussians at input pixels and lift them along camera rays, which makes primitive count and placement depend on image resolution and viewpoint. This reduces the scene-adaptive flexibility that makes classic 3DGS strong, often hurting quality and compactness.
method: Uses a feed-forward architecture that predicts 3D Gaussians more compactly than pixel-aligned approaches.
Introduces adaptive token expansion to allocate more primitives to under-reconstructed or complex regions.
Decouples primitive placement from raw input pixel locations so the model can better adapt to scene geometry and detail.
impact: For practitioners, this means faster and more memory-efficient 3D novel-view synthesis without sacrificing the adaptive detail allocation that improves rendering quality. It is especially relevant for deploying 3D reconstruction and view synthesis on limited hardware.

paper_title: ATSplat: Compact Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Adaptive Token Expansion
